newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka opposition MP killed in shootout.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka opposition MP killed in shootout.

text.p: A parliamentary deputy of Sri Lanka's main opposition United National Party (UNP) and five others were killed in an attack by gunmen near eastern Trincomalee town on Sunday, police said.
They said UNP member of parliament Mohammed Moharoof's vehicle was attacked on a stretch of road between Trincomalee and the nearby beach resort of Nilaveli at about 10.30 a.m. (0430 GMT).
The dead included Moharoof's driver, his bodyguard, a colleague, a principal of a local Moslem school and the driver's four-year-old son, police said.
Police blamed the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels for the killing, but declined to attribute a motive to the attack.
"We are still making inquiries," a police official said.
The LTTE are fighting a 13-year-old war for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war. The LTTE puts the toll higher.
UNP sources in the capital Colombo confirmed Moharoof had died in the attack, but they, too, stopped short of speculating why the lawmaker was killed.
Police said Moharoof was travelling in the Moslem-dominated area around Trincomalee, visiting villages where LTTE rebels had kidnapped fishermen in recent weeks.
They said the lawmaker had met with local police to discuss villagers' safety just before he was killed.
Moharoof, 58, was a deputy minister in the UNP government which lost power to the ruling People's Alliance in 1994.
He was the second parliamentary deputy to be killed this month in Trincomalee, 260 km (160 miles) east of Colombo.
Arunasalam Thangathurai, Trincomalee parliamentary deputy for the Tamil United Liberation Front (TULF), died in a grenade attack on July 5.
Thangathurai, who was killed while getting into his vehicle after inaugurating a new school building, was the eighth TULF leader to die in a series of political assassinations in as many years.
Four others, including the school principal, were also killed and 15 were wounded in the July 5 attack.
Police blamed the LTTE for Thangathurai's killing, but nobody has claimed responsibility for the attack.
